variants.headline: Looking back: party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by a party leader.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A party leader had blundered in an election debate.

A leader has blundered in a debate. Tempting material for a perfect quotation, except the words are not supplied here. The mistake is news enough. Readers can judge a performance without being given an invented audience, a fictional blush or a claim that the whole election is suddenly over.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate.
